hypothesis: Scaling backbone capacity to 1.75x width and upgrading multi-scale feature aggregation to Triple Pooling (Average + Generalized Mean p=3 + Max Pooling) across Stage 3 (8x8) and Stage 4 (4x4) creates a 4032-dimensional multi-scale descriptor that captures global context, salient mid-level visual structures, and sharp local peaks, significantly boosting SSL representation quality on CIFAR-100.
rationale: Iter 20 showed a dramatic jump (+4.2 pts to 0.6620) by concatenating Stage 3 and Stage 4 features, and Iter 23 showed that adding Max Pooling alongside Average Pooling (+0.13 pts to 0.6634) improved representations by capturing peak activations. Generalized Mean (GeM) Pooling with p=3 provides a smooth, non-linear activation metric that selectively highlights salient feature regions between Average (p=1) and Max (p=infinity) pooling. Combining Avg, GeM, and Max pooling across Stage 3 (448 channels) and Stage 4 (896 channels) at 1.75x width produces a rich 4032-dimensional standardized feature space well within memory and compute bounds (~50 min run time).
expected_effect: Increases linear probe validation accuracy beyond 0.6634 by providing richer feature capacity and multi-aspect pooling signatures across mid-level (8x8) and high-level (4x4) spatial feature maps.
change_summary: 1. Scaled Anti-Aliased ResNet-26 width multiplier from 1.5x to 1.75x (channels [112, 224, 448, 896]). 2. Introduced GeMPool2d (p=3.0) and built a Triple Pooling pipeline (AvgPool + GeMPool + MaxPool) for both Stage 3 (448-dim) and Stage 4 (896-dim), generating a 4032-dimensional feature vector. 3. Updated ProjectionHead input dimension to 4032 (4032 -> 4096 -> 4096 -> 2048). 4. Preserved top-performing Joint DCL + Barlow Twins loss and detail-preserving CIFAR augmentations.
